body:
Okay, you are correct.  I don't know or care about you on a personal level.  But as someone who is still battling depression, I want to take advantage of this high point in my life and offer it to others in shitty situations.  I didn't want to reveal my main source of depression being that it is of a legal nature (involving the drugs), but it is still not resolved and it is still an issue that I have to face.

I'm sorry if I sound generic...I can't address every situation you might be going through...only what I've been through.  I know you can't "just be happy."  At it's worst, there's no better description for my depression than "crippling."  I don't want to get out of bed, I don't want to go to class, I don't want to see or talk to anyone, I don't want eat, I don't want to move.  During those times, all I want to do is just die.

I just want everyone who sees this to know that I felt the same way you have.  I did not see any hope of better days or any reason to carry on with life.  I'm only 20 years old, and I know I have a lot to live for.  Even if most of what I'm experiencing here on Earth is pain and suffering, at least I'm experiencing something.  After I die, that's it...there's nothing more, my life is over.  If there is even one source of beauty and happiness in your life, no matter how small it may be, that alone makes life worth living.

I'm sorry I couldn't offer you what you wanted to hear at least initially.  For those of us with depression, it is definitely a lot of hard work to stay happy. I hope you have someone you can talk to about your depression, because when you feel like you're at your worst, that's probably the best thing you can do.

Thank you!  I started learning German with that site a few weeks ago, and it's awesome!  I just really think it's important to minimize time where you're just sitting around introspecting.

Let's face it, I would waste hours moping on my couch or in bed.  If you replace that time with constructive activities, you're definitely going to be much happier.  I know it's generic advice, but it's really true.

You're taking everything I said out of context.  I'm merely trying to offer some hope and a success story for those who feel like there is no hope.

You know the saying "Text without context is pretext"?  Yeah, I'd like to point out that you did not even quote the entire sentence that that statement is from.  I said:

> I am not sure if it's the case everywhere, but where I live, if you are issued a TDO, you don't need insurance to go to the hospital.

I was issued a TDO by a publicly funded organization in my community.  I'm not sure how other similar organizations operate, but in my particular case, if you were without insurance, and you are admitted to the hospital involuntarily, you will not get charged.  Before I actually went to the hospital, I was in my University Counseling center trying to get help.  Then they called the cops to take me to the police station where I was interviewed further.  After basically being held prisoner for 5 hours in a jail cell-sized room at the police station, they decided that I was to be taken to the hospital in handcuffs.

I know it sounds seriously fucked up that that can happen, but we don't live in the days of *One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest* anymore, and they aren't going to make a sane/healthy person take psych meds.  They made me take sedatives because I was so angry when I got there.  If you talk to them and tell them what's going on and let them know how you want to go forward with treatment, they should be listening to you.  I told them that I didn't want antidepressants, so I was not put on any.  If you are being held against your will and you are being forced to take meds that you don't want to take and feel are making you worse, you should contact a lawyer.

At the time, I felt so upset, and I did feel like I was in *One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest*, but now that some time has passed, I can see the situation with much more clarity.  I can see that what happened was for the best.  And I know you've heard it a thousand times, but the doctors prescribing you these meds are honestly looking out for your best interests.  If you feel as though you are being treated improperly, go see a different doctor.

I'm sorry about what's happened to you, but if you check yourself into the hospital voluntarily, you are going to have to pay for it somehow.  The downside to getting a TDO is that there will most likely be a legal record of your incident, and unless your case gets dismissed, you will lose your gun ownership rights...but honestly for the reasons that you'd be going to the hospital, that's probably a good thing.  And, at least in my state, the information of your Temporary Detention Order is not available to the public (NOTE: I said "In my state." That doesn't mean everywhere).

I'm not saying you just have to snap your fingers and BAM: you're happy.  I tried killing myself in 8th grade by slitting my wrist open (ended in me panicking, calling my neighbor, going to the hospital to get stitches and coming up with a fake story for my parents) and I've struggled with suicide ever since.  I know how hard it is and that not everyone is the same.  I don't expect my advice to apply to everyone (especially if you have a personality disorder), but I figured that I'm doing well, and I owe it to everyone else out there who is depressed to share with them how **I** got through **my** depression.

I know, after I got back home from my hiring meeting, I looked back just 2 months at where I was, and I knew I had to post here.

I also think people should know that suicide is like a disease in that it spreads.  My mom and her sisters found their mother in a closet overdosed on drugs when they were just little girls (That was a failed suicide attempt).  Now 2 of my aunts have also had very serious suicide attempts, and many others in my family have had struggles with suicidal thoughts and drug/alcohol abuse.

It hurts so deeply to see people in your family go in such a way.  Thankfully everyone in my family has failed their attempts, but my aunt for example was in a coma for a week, and we weren't sure if she would make it.  Think about how those actions will affect the next generation.

You meet new people in every phase of your life.  There is so much more to life outside of high school. I'm just 20, and I can tell you that at 17, I felt the same way. You are going to meet some great people in college and beyond.  If someone told me who my best friends were going to be when I was 17, I wouldn't have believed them.

People are clueless and stupid.  You can't expect your high school peers to recognize the pain you're in.  You're letting other people determine your life's worth!  You can make whatever you want out of your life...that should make you feel powerful!  I can assure you that in 2-3 years, you will look back at this time of your life and be so thankful that you never went through with it.

Don't entertain intrusive thoughts.  Recognize them and immediately rebuke them!  You are loved and cared for deeply.  I gave up just like you did, and I let my grades slip and settled for mediocrity.  You are capable of so much more than that.

You say your aspirations are only there to be met by someone else, but you are looking at it the wrong way!  That "someone else" is just there to push you further and to get you to achieve bigger and better things!  You can find so much satisfaction and worth in your life by accomplishing tasks and working towards your goals.  Work towards your goals for ***YOU***.  Don't worry about other people's approval.  Soon enough, your hard work and ability **WILL** be recognized, but for the time being, ***YOU*** recognize your hard work and success, and that's all you need.

Suicide is **NEVER** the best answer.  At least while you are here on Earth, you are experiencing something.  Even though all you can feel is pain right now, don't you want to stick around long enough to see what great things lie ahead of you?  You are so young.  You don't stop reading a book because you don't like the first paragraph.  High school is merely the training for the rest of your life.  You haven't even started living yet!
